source: DITHER / DITHER2 SLOT 7 - I/O AND HGR SUPPORT

symbols.name: COMMENT_DITH_SYNC_THR
symbols.comment: DITHER slot 7: RD returns video-sync state in D7 ($00 low, $80 high) and stops capture; WR stops capture and latches the 8-bit threshold. V1 uses the threshold for monochrome capture; V2 retains it and uses it for luminance-source fallback.

symbols.name: COMMENT_DITH_CAPTURE
symbols.comment: DITHER slot 7: RD enables capture and copies a frame into the currently selected HGR page; emulator return value is $00. WR is ignored. V1 outputs monochrome bits 0-6; V2 preserves supplied HGR color phase bit 7.

symbols.name: COMMENT_VIDEO_GRAPHICS
symbols.comment: Apple II motherboard soft switch: select graphics display; pair with HIRES and the desired page for HGR.

symbols.name: COMMENT_VIDEO_TEXT
symbols.comment: Apple II motherboard soft switch: select text display; this is not a DITHER threshold or capture register.

symbols.name: COMMENT_VIDEO_FULL
symbols.comment: Apple II motherboard soft switch: disable mixed text/graphics mode and display a full graphics screen.

symbols.name: COMMENT_VIDEO_MIXED
symbols.comment: Apple II motherboard soft switch: enable mixed graphics/text display; the digitizer still captures its full HGR frame.

symbols.name: COMMENT_VIDEO_PAGE1
symbols.comment: Apple II motherboard soft switch: select video page 1; both DITHER drivers follow this page state and target HGR RAM at $2000.

symbols.name: COMMENT_VIDEO_PAGE2
symbols.comment: Apple II motherboard soft switch: select video page 2; both DITHER drivers follow this page state and target HGR RAM at $4000.

symbols.name: COMMENT_VIDEO_LORES
symbols.comment: Apple II motherboard soft switch: select low-resolution graphics display; the DITHER drivers write HGR buffers rather than a private lores buffer.

symbols.name: COMMENT_VIDEO_HIRES
symbols.comment: Apple II motherboard soft switch: select high-resolution graphics display; captured data uses Apple II HGR memory layout.

symbols.name: COMMENT_HGR_PAGE1
symbols.comment: First address of the page-1 HGR buffer ($2000-$3FFF); selected by VIDEO_PAGE1. Scan lines use the Apple II interleaved layout rather than consecutive linear rows.

symbols.name: COMMENT_HGR_PAGE2
symbols.comment: First address of the page-2 HGR buffer ($4000-$5FFF); selected by VIDEO_PAGE2. V2 preserves the HGR color-phase bit when copying a prepared page.

notes: All 16 slot-7 offsets are named. Only $C0F0 and $C0F8 implement card operations in the current DITHER and DITHER2 drivers; 14 offsets are explicitly unused.
This table covers both current emulator variants and distinguishes RD/WR behavior in each comment. The color converter controls in the host UI are not guest-visible slot registers.
VIDEO_* symbols are shared Apple II motherboard switches, not registers on the DITHER card. HGR_PAGE1/2 label only the two buffer base addresses, not every byte in their RAM pages.
Read-only debugger peeks (ctx.bRO=true) do not stop or start capture. Ordinary emulated CPU reads have the side effects described in the comments.
No DSCAN RAM entry-point labels are invented: those would need a separate instruction-pc table for the exact loaded software version.
For another slot s, relocate only $C0F0-$C0FF using base=$C080+$10*s. The shared VIDEO_* and HGR_PAGE* addresses do not move.
The unused-offset and sync-value claims describe the current RetroAppleJS drivers, rather than undocumented electrical behavior of every historical board.
